set.body:
Defect: D6 + D1/D2. The crosswalk exists THREE times: docs/data/sherlock/timebase-repair.json, literals at acquire/.../sherlock.scala:45-67, and SherlockAnnotationsSuite.scala:188-199 -- a test NAMED 'the pinned nn2017 manifest carries the crosswalk constants of timebase-repair.json v2' that NEVER OPENS THE JSON and asserts Scala literals against Scala literals. It cannot fail for the reason its name gives. The binding derivation exists only in prose: playbackEndTicks 3565000 + uncoveredTailTicks 500 = durationTicks 3565500 (part B: 3860000 + 27000 = 3887000).

Do: Read the values from the JSON, including that derivation. Replace the suite with a test that OPENS the JSON. AND GO ONE STEP FURTHER AT NO COST: ClockRepair.of needs a SourceDerivationReceipt (source.scala:480-495: algorithm, parameters, inputChecksums), and the JSON already carries every input checksum -- the annotation sha and both media shas. So construct a REAL ClockRepair (scale 2500/1, offset 0, one per part) instead of literals. That is the proof that D1/D2's dead vocabulary is reachable, and it should be this slice's headline.

Tests: The whole slice is ONE behaviour: change a value in timebase-repair.json and the suite goes red. Write it to compare PARSED against USED, or the mutation still will not bite.

Mutants (SD1 — each must die, recorded by name): change a value in the JSON -> the suite must go red (today: nothing happens). Reinstate a literal in the Scala -> the JSON-comparison test must fail.

Exit: Editing a source record breaks a test, and ClockRepair has its first production caller.

Plan: docs/plans/2026-09-17-annotation-intake-contract.md S3, P5
set.title: intake P5: replace the transcribed Sherlock crosswalk with a JSON-read ClockRepair
